::: {.lead}
Backgammon's strongest engines were built in the 1990s. Raccoon is a rebuild
with the methods that have since transformed chess and Go — a deep residual
network trained by large-scale distillation — and it runs entirely in your
browser. No account, no server, nothing to install.
:::

::: {.raccoon-app data-mode="play"}
:::

::: {.app-fallback}
The board above needs JavaScript and WebAssembly. Everything else on this site
works without them, and the engine also runs [in a terminal](engine.qmd).
:::

## What it does

- **Play** a full cubeless money game against the engine — [full-size board](play.qmd).
- **Analyse** any position: ranked candidate moves, cubeless equity, and the
  win/gammon/backgammon split — [open the analyser](analyse.qmd).
- **Bring your own positions** with XGID import and export, the format XG and
  GNU Backgammon already speak.

Everything happens on your machine: the network's weights are downloaded once
and evaluated locally, so nothing you play is ever sent anywhere.

## How strong is it

Scored on the BGSage money benchmark — {{< var engine.pr_n >}} checker decisions
with rollout-quality references. PR is mean move-selection error × 500; lower is
better.

| Engine | Compute per decision | PR ({{< var engine.pr_n >}} decisions) |
|---|---|---|
| GNU Backgammon, 2-ply full-width search | ~1.3 s | **{{< var engine.gnubg_2ply_pr >}}** |
| **Raccoon, single network evaluation** | ~10 ms | **{{< var engine.pr >}}** |
| GNU Backgammon, single network evaluation | ~10 ms | **{{< var engine.gnubg_0ply_pr >}}** |

At equal cost Raccoon's checker play is well past GNU Backgammon's own network,
and it has closed most of the distance to GNU Backgammon's 2-ply search while
doing no search at all. In direct play it wins {{< var engine.ppg_edge >}} points
per game against GNU Backgammon at 0-ply over {{< var engine.ppg_n >}} games —
measured with [variance-reduced rollouts](https://research.raccoonbg.com/variance_reduction.html),
which read the same games seven times more precisely than counting points does.

The engine in your browser is the measured engine, not a cut-down version of it:
the exported network scores PR 0.9500 on the benchmark against 0.9498 for the
PyTorch checkpoint it came from.

The honest caveat: this is **checker play only, cubeless**. The doubling cube —
half of competitive backgammon — is the next milestone.
